text: Before anything else in Fabric happens, you need a workspace — let's create one.

New workspace, name it, assign it a capacity — a trial, or a paid F-SKU — and apply. Unlike Databricks, there's no VM size or runtime version to configure. The capacity assignment is the only compute decision, and it's made once, at the workspace level.

Roles are simpler too. Admin can do everything, including workspace settings. Member can create, edit, and share. Contributor can create and edit, but not share. Viewer is read-only. A simpler, coarser cousin of Unity Catalog's grant and revoke.

And this should feel familiar — a workspace is the same top-level container idea, capacity is the compute clusters used to provide, and roles are a coarser grant and revoke. Same shape, different name.
One container, one compute decision, simpler roles. Next lesson: OneLake, one lake for the whole organization.
